text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG

- Unrest in the Christian Democrats (CDU) as Kurt Biedenkopf, premier of Saxony state and a long-time critic of Chancellor Helmut Kohl, tells party general secretary Peter Hintze in a letter that Kohl's candidacy is a "particular risk" for the party.
- German President Roman Herzog calls on political leaders, business and social elites to show courage and decisiveness and stop hesitating about long overdue reforms.
- Chancellor Kohl says the timetable for the introduction of a European single currency must be maintained.
HANDELSBLATT
- Bundesbank head Hans Tietmeyer and Finance Minister Theo Waigel, speaking in Washington on the sidelines of the G7 summit, underscore Germany's interest in a strong deutschemark.

- Opposition Social Democrat (SPD) premiers of federal states distance themselves from SPD party leader Oskar Lafontaine after talks with the ruling coaltion over planned tax reforms broke down last week.
- CDU general secretary Peter Hinze supports comments made by President Herzog urging politicians to pursue much needed reforms.
- A leading German industrial group and an energy company are intersted in taking over collapsed German shipbuilder Bremer Vulkan.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Indignation in Kohl's CDU after criticism by Saxony premier Biedenkopf of Kohl's decision to run again as chancellor candidate in next year's general elections.
- Federal Labour Office president Bernhard Jagoda says will need a significantly higher federal subsidy because of high unemployment despite Bonn's need to keep save.
- Bavaria's premier Edmund Stoiber says parts of planned tax reform not sensible.
DIE WELT
- German President Herzog appeals for a unified move into the 21st century and says urgent reforms must be carried out.
- Saxony premier Biedenkopf under pressure after criticism of Chancellor Kohl.
- Tax reforms sparks weekend of disagreement within the opposition SPD and the ruling coalition.
- Dispute in Frankfurt over plans by Dresdner Bank to build a second, 190 metre high, skyscraper.
